subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style calculation on quantitative chemistry, then mark my answer against the CCEA spec.
promptWeak: Explain quantitative chemistry for GCSE CCEA Chemistry simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: What is the relative formula mass (Mr) of water, H2O? (Ar: H=1, O=16)
What is the Mr of calcium carbonate, CaCO3? (Ar: Ca=40, C=12, O=16)
What is the Mr of sulfuric acid, H2SO4? (Ar: H=1, S=32, O=16)
One mole of any substance contains the same number of particles, given by:
questions.explain: One mole contains 6.02 x 10^23 particles, known as the Avogadro constant.

questions.q: How many moles are in 80 g of sodium hydroxide, NaOH? (Mr = 40)
How many moles are in 36 g of water, H2O? (Mr = 18)
What is the mass of 0.25 mol of calcium carbonate, CaCO3? (Mr = 100)
questions.explain: Mass = moles x Mr = 0.25 x 100 = 25 g.

questions.q: What is the mass of 3 mol of carbon dioxide, CO2? (Mr = 44)
questions.explain: Mass = moles x Mr = 3 x 44 = 132 g.

questions.q: What is the percentage by mass of oxygen in water, H2O? (Mr = 18, O=16)
What is the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate, NH4NO3? (Mr = 80, N=14)
The empirical formula of a compound is:
options: The simplest whole number ratio of atoms of each element
The actual number of atoms in a molecule
Always the same as the molecular formula
questions.explain: The empirical formula is the simplest whole number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.

questions.q: A compound contains 2.4 g carbon and 0.6 g hydrogen. (Ar: C=12, H=1) What is its empirical formula?
A molecule has empirical formula CH2 and Mr = 42. (CH2 = 14) What is its molecular formula?
questions.explain: 42 / 14 = 3, so the molecular formula is 3 x (CH2) = C3H6.

questions.q: In 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO, what mass of magnesium oxide forms from 48 g of magnesium? (Ar: Mg=24, O=16)
questions.explain: Moles Mg = 48/24 = 2. Ratio Mg:MgO is 2:2 = 1:1, so 2 mol MgO. Mr of MgO = 40, mass = 2 x 40 = 80 g.

questions.q: In N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3, how many moles of hydrogen are needed to react fully with 2 mol of nitrogen?
questions.explain: The ratio N2:H2 is 1:3, so 2 mol N2 needs 2 x 3 = 6 mol H2.

questions.q: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 50 g but only 40 g is obtained. What is the percentage yield?
Which is NOT a reason a percentage yield is less than 100%?
options: Product is lost when separated from the mixture
The reaction is reversible and does not go to completion
The balanced equation was written correctly
questions.explain: Losses on separation, reversible reactions and side reactions all reduce yield. A correctly balanced equation does not reduce yield.

questions.q: What is the concentration (in g/dm3) of a solution containing 20 g of solute in 0.5 dm3?
How many molecules are in 2 mol of a substance? (Avogadro constant = 6.02 x 10^23)
questions.explain: Number of particles = moles x Avogadro constant = 2 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 1.204 x 10^24.
